about: The camera library (Erick 2026-10-17: 'a proper list of camera positions and movements, like a library … metadata that tells us what is the best used content for such take, redundancy is welcomed so we can choose … just choose the take and the length'). A shot row says {"take": "<id>", ...overrides} and its seconds; everything here is a default the row may change. Values given as [a, b] move from a to b over the shot (eased, with 'hold' seconds still at each end); single values stay. Points and bearings come from the film's site file (sites/<site>/site.json). Positions: eye = target + (bearing, dist) on the ground, 'height' above the ground there; bearing is FROM the target TO the eye, degrees from true north. Look: 'target' (at look_h above the target's ground), 'dir' (az, el), 'sun' (the frame's own Sun or Moon, el offset), 'down' (straight down on the target). Lens = vertical field of view in degrees.

locked_tele_on_axis.best_for: the alignment itself: a body (Sun/Moon) framed by stones on a line; time-lapse of the body crossing the frame
locked_tele_on_axis.avoid: establishing a place; anything that needs the viewer to know where we are first

locked_tele_window.best_for: the Sun inside one gap seen from the centre (the window shot); the climax still
locked_tele_window.avoid: showing that it is an axis — pair it with an axis or overhead take before

locked_eye_level_wide.best_for: the monument in its land at human height; sky and clouds changing over the stones
locked_eye_level_wide.avoid: precise alignments (too wide to read a degree)

locked_overhead.best_for: shadows as a clock and a compass; the sundial; contrast between days at the same Sun height

overhead_rise.best_for: opening out from the circle to the earthwork while shadows lengthen

overhead_fall.best_for: closing in on the circle, ending on the stones (a wide that hands over to a medium)

overhead_turn.best_for: a held instant seen from above, the frame turning until the axis is vertical in picture

axis_push_in.best_for: making an alignment evident by parallax: the gaps line up as the camera closes in on the line

axis_push_in_reverse.best_for: the same push from the other end of the axis (the winter sunset); the MATCH of axis_push_in

axis_pull_out.best_for: after the climax: leaving the held instant along the line, the land opening behind

axis_crane_up.best_for: revealing the whole axis from the circle to the Heel Stone and the Avenue: rise behind the trilithon, tilt down along the line

axis_crane_down.best_for: settling from above onto the line at eye height just as the body appears (a wide→medium bridge)

truck_across_axis.best_for: showing a line by sliding across it: the gaps open, align for an instant, and close (the eye feels the line)

line_tele_station.best_for: a line drawn by two markers (Station Stones): stand behind one, look past the other at the body

sun_track_tele.best_for: the body itself moving behind the stones; the camera keeps the disc in frame
sun_track_tele.avoid: proving a fixed line (the frame moves with the body)

orbit_quarter_low.best_for: showing the stones as a structure: the camera walks a quarter circle round them at eye height

orbit_half_high.best_for: the circle and its earthwork from 60 m up, the Sun's light moving across them

orbit_full_slow.best_for: a held instant all round (time stopped), e.g. the alignment moment from every side

flyover_high.best_for: establishing: the Plain and the monument small in it (frame top stays under the data edge)
flyover_high.avoid: horizons (from height the LiDAR edge shows)

descend_to_eye.best_for: a wide→medium bridge: from above the circle down to eye height on the axis

walk_avenue.best_for: arriving as people did: along the Avenue toward the circle at eye height

walk_out_to_sun.best_for: leaving the circle along the axis toward the rising body

inside_look_up.best_for: the sky over the trilithons: stars turning, clouds passing, the lintels as a frame
